Location Name: Ponte dei Baretteri (Sede dell'Accademia dei Granelleschi)
Specific Location / Address: Ponte dei Baretteri / Merceria San Zulian
Description & Significance: Historic bridge in the Mercerie where Daniele Farsetti, Gasparo Gozzi, and Carlo Gozzi gathered in a workshop to found the satirical Accademia dei Granelleschi.
Key Historical Context: Giuseppe Tassini recounts in detail the foundation of the humorous literary academy: 'Avendo Daniele Farsetti, ed altri amici, ascoltato nel 1747, in Convento dei Frari, un certo padre predicatore comporre versi bislacchi... decisero di fondare una scherzevole adunanza.' The academy aimed to defend classical Italian poetry against modern French corruptions.
Exact Quotation from Tassini: Avendo Daniele Farsetti, ed altri amici, ascoltato nel 1747, in Convento dei Frari, un certo padre predicatore... decisero di fondare una scherzevole adunanza.
English Translation & Toponymic Analysis: Daniele Farsetti and friends, having heard an eccentric preacher in 1747 at the Frari convent, decided to found a playful assembly to mock pedantic and corrupt literature.

Location Name: Chiesa e Convento di Santa Maria del Pianto (Collegio De Martiis)
Description & Significance: 17th-century octagonal church and monastery complex at the eastern end of Fondamente Nove, acquired in 1814 by philosophy master Abate Antonio De Martiis.
Key Historical Context: Tassini documents how the complex passed from De Martiis to Abate Daniele Canal, who established a charity boarding school for impoverished young girls: 'v’istituì altro collegio, ove si educano povere fanciulle, e, dopo un breve spazio di tempo, giunse a riaprire la chiesa, riconsacrata il 21 agosto 1851' [Tassini 130].
Exact Quotation from Tassini: v’istituì altro collegio, ove si educano povere fanciulle, e, dopo un breve spazio di tempo, giunse a riaprire la chiesa, riconsacrata il 21 agosto 1851.
English Translation & Toponymic Analysis: He established there another boarding school where poor young girls were educated, and shortly thereafter succeeded in reopening the church, reconsecrated on August 21, 1851.

Location Name: Teatro di San Cassiano / Area di Rialto (Burchiella)
Specific Location / Address: Campo San Cassiano / Calle della Commedia
Description & Significance: Theatrical stage and literary circle of Antonio Molino, known as 'Il Burchiella', founder of Venetian dialect comic theatre.
Key Historical Context: In his study on Venetian festivities, Tassini records the performances of Burchiella, noting that he created popular theatrical spectacles where he 'parlava in lingua Greca e Schiavona corrotta coll’Italiana' [Tassini, Feste... 101], mimicking Levantines, Greeks, and Slavic mariners.
Exact Quotation from Tassini: parlava in lingua Greca e Schiavona corrotta coll’Italiana.
English Translation & Toponymic Analysis: He spoke in a hybrid Greek and Slavic dialect corrupted with Italian, delighting Venetian carnival crowds.

Location Name: Ca’ Corner della Ca’ Granda
Description & Significance: Monumental High Renaissance patrician palace designed by Jacopo Sansovino on the Grand Canal, replacing the previous palace destroyed by fire.
Key Historical Context: Tassini records that before Sansovino's reconstruction, the earlier Gothic palace burned down on August 16, 1532, and was originally built in the 15th century by wealthy citizen Bartolommeo Malombra [Tassini 185]. Scamozzi later completed the upper attic.
Tassini Work Cited: Alcuni palazzi ed antichi edifizii / Curiosità Veneziane
Exact Quotation from Tassini: residenza dei Corner, eretta nel secolo precedente dal ricchissimo cittadino Bartolommeo Malombra e portata a termine dallo Scamozzi.
English Translation & Toponymic Analysis: Residence of the Corner family, erected in the previous century by the very wealthy citizen Bartolommeo Malombra and brought to completion by Scamozzi.

Location Name: Gran Caffè Quadri (Insegna del Rimedio)
Description & Significance: Historic café in Piazza San Marco established under the Procuratie Vecchie, originally a licensed shop selling Malvasia wine.
Key Historical Context: Tassini relates that the café was initially named 'Il Rimedio' because starting in 1638 the shop sold Malvasia wine, which was popular and officially classified as a medicinal remedy believed to reinvigorate human strength: 'fin dal 1638 vi si vendeva il vino Malvasia ritenuto all’epoca un rimedio in quanto si credeva rinvigorisse le forze umane' [Tassini]. In 1775 Giorgio Quadri converted it into an upscale coffeehouse.
Exact Quotation from Tassini: fin dal 1638 vi si vendeva il vino Malvasia ritenuto all’epoca un rimedio in quanto si credeva rinvigorisse le forze umane.
English Translation & Toponymic Analysis: Ever since 1638 Malvasia wine was sold there, regarded at the time as a medicine because it was believed to invigorate the human body.

Location Name: Corte Casolo (Famiglia Casolo)
Description & Significance: Ancient toponym and urban courtyard linked to the ancient tribunizia Casolo family from Altino.
Key Historical Context: Tassini documents in his study on Venetian capital crimes and nobility that the Casolo family originated in Altino and was admitted to the Maggior Consiglio in 1089 [Tassini, Condanne... 19].
Exact Quotation from Tassini: Famiglia tribunizia, proveniente da Altino, ascritta al M.C. nel 1089.
English Translation & Toponymic Analysis: Tribunizial family originating from Altino, admitted to the Great Council in 1089.

Location Name: Castello Ducale (Palazzo Ducale)
Description & Significance: The fortified ducal castle established by Doge Angelo Partecipazio, surrounded by moat waters.
Key Historical Context: Tassini traces the architectural chronology and master builders of the Palazzo Ducale over the centuries, listing: 'Baseggio, Calendario, i Bon, Rizzo, Pietro Lombardo, da Ponte, Scarpagnino e altri' [Tassini 378].
Exact Quotation from Tassini: Seguendo i periodi della costruzione nei suoi particolari si rileva che durante i secoli in cui si svolsero i lavori furono nominati proti dell’opera: Baseggio, Calendario, i Bon, Rizzo...
English Translation & Toponymic Analysis: Following the construction phases in detail shows that over centuries of works, the proto architects included Baseggio, Calendario, the Bon family, Rizzo, and Lombardo.

Location Name: Piazzetta San Marco (Luogo della Congiura Bocconio)
Description & Significance: Site of public execution for Marin Bocconio and his fellow conspirators following the Serrata del Maggior Consiglio.
Key Historical Context: According to a legend recorded by Giuseppe Tassini, the conspiracy was betrayed unintentionally by Bocconio himself, who murmured about the plot inside a church and was overheard: 'Secondo una leggenda ricordata da Giuseppe Tassini a tradire i congiurati fu involontariamente lo stesso Bocconio che parlottandone in chiesa si fece sentire.' The 12 conspirators were hanged between the columns of the Piazzetta.
Exact Quotation from Tassini: Secondo una leggenda ricordata da Giuseppe Tassini a tradire i congiurati fu involontariamente lo stesso Bocconio che parlottandone in chiesa si fece sentire.
English Translation & Toponymic Analysis: According to a legend recorded by Tassini, Bocconio himself unintentionally betrayed the plot by speaking of it inside a church where he was overheard.

Location Name: Calle Dolce / Palazzo Dolce
Description & Significance: Calle and residential seat of the ancient Dolce family, originating from Lombardy.
Key Historical Context: Tassini notes in his study of capital sentences that the original patrician branch of the Dolce family became extinct in 1248, while a non-patrician branch produced prominent intellectual and playwright Ludovico Dolce [Tassini, Condanne... 23].
Exact Quotation from Tassini: Famiglia, originaria della Lombardia, estintasi nel 1248 [Cfr. Tassini, Condanne... 23].
English Translation & Toponymic Analysis: Family originating from Lombardy, whose patrician line extinguished in 1248 according to Tassini's capital records.

Location Name: Libreria Editrice Filippi
Specific Location / Address: Calle della Casseleria / Calle del Paradiso, 5456
Description & Significance: Historic Venetian publishing house responsible for rescuing and reprinting Giuseppe Tassini's foundational historical works in the 20th century.
Key Historical Context: Publisher Luciano Filippi revived Venetian antiquarian literature by publishing reprints of Tassini's *Feste Veneziane* (1959) and *Curiosità Veneziane*, making Tassini's toponymic research universally accessible to modern scholars.
Exact Quotation from Tassini: Nel 1956 Luciano aprì una sua libreria, avviando (1959) anche una sua attività editoriale con la ristampa di Feste Veneziane del Tassini...
English Translation & Toponymic Analysis: In 1959 Luciano Filippi launched his publishing activity with the reprint of Tassini's Venetian Festivities and Curiosità Veneziane.

Location Name: Lido di Venezia (Sito del Duello Galli-Macola)
Description & Significance: Secluded dunes on the Lido where aristocratic and student duels were secretly fought in the late 19th century.
Key Historical Context: Following the duel on May 2, 1894, between university student Galli and newspaper editor Ferruccio Macola, Giuseppe Tassini expressed indignation in *Curiosità Veneziane*, questioning how illegal duels forbidden by the Penal Code could be announced days in advance without authorities intervening [Tassini, Curiosità ... XXVI].
Exact Quotation from Tassini: Ora come va che si compiono, annunziati anche qualche giorno prima, in barba all’autorità.
English Translation & Toponymic Analysis: How is it that these duels take place, announced even days beforehand, in open defiance of the authorities?

Location Name: Giardini Pubblici di Castello (Quartiere di Sant'Antonio Abate)
Description & Significance: Napoleonic public park created by demolishing an entire maritime quarter, four churches, and three monasteries.
Key Historical Context: Tassini provides a poignant account of the demolition ordered by Napoleon: 'Ad ottenere lo spazio necessario, si distrussero le parrocchie di S. Nicolò di Castello e di S. Maria delle Vergini, i due conventi di S. Domenico... il convento della Concezione di M.V. o delle Cappuccine, e la chiesa e il convento di S. Antonio Abate' [Tassini, Curiosità ... 277].
Exact Quotation from Tassini: Ad ottenere lo spazio necessario, si distrussero le parrocchie di S. Nicolò di Castello e di S. Maria delle Vergini, i due conventi di S. Domenico... e la chiesa e il convento di S. Antonio Abate.
English Translation & Toponymic Analysis: To obtain the necessary space, the parishes of San Nicolò di Castello and Santa Maria delle Vergini were destroyed, along with two Dominican convents and the church and monastery of Sant'Antonio Abate.

Location Name: Piazza San Marco e Canal Grande (Giostre Cavalleresche)
Specific Location / Address: Piazza San Marco / Bacino di San Marco
Description & Significance: Civic arena where historical tournaments and aquatic jousts were staged for dogal celebrations.
Key Historical Context: Tassini details chivalric jousts in Venice, including the May 30, 1242 tournament and the February 1491 joust staged on the frozen Grand Canal and Bacino before Queen Caterina Cornaro, where Stradiot cavalry ran tilting matches on wooden platforms [Tassini, Feste].
Exact Quotation from Tassini: infine la giostra svoltasi nel 1491, non in Piazza, al cospetto di Caterina Cornaro, quando alcuni Stradiotti apparati di tutto punto corsero la giostra...
English Translation & Toponymic Analysis: Finally the joust held in 1491 before Caterina Cornaro, when Stradiot mercenaries fully equipped ran tournament tilts on the water.

Location Name: Bottega Talamini sul Ponte di Rialto
Description & Significance: 18th-century apothecary shop on the Rialto Bridge renowned throughout Europe for creating lifelike botanical wax fruit.
Key Historical Context: Tassini records from archival chronicles that on April 17, 1757, apothecary Giambattista Talamini perfected an ingenious secret paste formula allowing him to craft wax fruit so realistic that buyers could not distinguish them from real fruit [Tassini].
Exact Quotation from Tassini: Egli, mediante un suo segreto, lavorava paste cerose in guisa di frutti, con tanta perfezione da ingannare la vista dei più accorti.
English Translation & Toponymic Analysis: Through his trade secret, he crafted wax pastes into fruit shapes with such perfection that they deceived even the keenest observer.

Location Name: Casa di Giuseppe Tassini (Lapide Commemorativa)
Description & Significance: Ancestral townhouse of Giuseppe Tassini, bearing the official marble plaque dedicated to the author of 'Curiosità Veneziane'.
Key Historical Context: Tassini spent his life here researching Venetian archives. He published *Curiosità Veneziane* in 1863, *Edifici di Venezia distrutti*, *Alcuni palazzi ed antichi edifizii*, *Condanne capitali*, and *Feste Veneziane*. On his death in 1899, the city remembered him as the greatest investigator of Venetian popular traditions.
Exact Quotation from Tassini: IN QUESTA CASA ABITÒ GIUSEPPE TASSINI AUTORE DELLE “CURIOSITÀ VENEZIANE” APPASSIONATO RICERCATORE DELLE NOSTRE TRADIZIONI 1827 – 1899.
English Translation & Toponymic Analysis: In this house lived Giuseppe Tassini, author of Curiosità Veneziane, passionate researcher of our traditions (1827–1899).

Location Name: Piazza San Marco e Ridotto (Uso delle Maschere)
Description & Significance: Civic zones where Venetian masks (bauta, moretta, larva) were worn during six months of the year.
Key Historical Context: Tassini traces the social and political psychology of masks in Venice, citing the Maggior Consiglio laws forbidding armed masks and nocturnal disguises, and documenting how masks transformed social hierarchies across the city [Tassini, Feste].
Exact Quotation from Tassini: La maschera a Venezia non è solo sinonimo di Carnevale, ma invade la vita sociale... Tassini documenta le restrizioni dei Dieci.
English Translation & Toponymic Analysis: In Venice the mask was not merely a Carnival prop, but an everyday instrument of social life regulated by the Council of Ten.

Location Name: Calle de le Muneghe (Abitazione di Matteo Lovat)
Description & Significance: Narrow street in Cannaregio where shoemaker Matteo Lovat enacted his notorious public self-crucifixion on July 19, 1805.
Key Historical Context: Tassini records the sensational event: 'messosi a nudo, cintosi il capo di spine, e fattasi con un coltello la ferita nel costato... calatosi penzoloni per dare spettacolo del proprio martirio ai passanti' [Tassini, Curiosità ... 439]. Lovat was rescued and transferred to San Servolo hospital.
Exact Quotation from Tassini: messosi a nudo, cintosi il capo di spine, e fattasi con un coltello la ferita nel costato... calatosi penzoloni per dare spettacolo del proprio martirio ai passanti.
English Translation & Toponymic Analysis: Having stripped naked, crowned his head with thorns, and stabbed himself in the rib, he suspended himself from his window to stage his martyrdom for passersby.

Location Name: Campi di Venezia (Luoghi delle Momarie)
Specific Location / Address: Campo San Polo / Rio di San Polo
Description & Significance: Public squares where 'momarie'—grotesque allegorical masquerades and pantomimes—were staged for noble wedding feasts.
Key Historical Context: Tassini explains that 'momarie' or 'bombarie' were silent costumed theatrical pantomimes performed on decorated boats and open campi, popular during patrician celebrations until prohibited due to rowdy excesses [Tassini, Feste].
Exact Quotation from Tassini: mascherate o giullerie, ovvero parodie satiriche che in origine si facevano in occasione di banchetti nuziali.
English Translation & Toponymic Analysis: Pantomimes and satirical parodies originally staged on the occasion of patrician wedding feasts.

Location Name: Palazzo Pasqualini
Description & Significance: Patrician-style residence on the Cannaregio Canal built by the Pasqualini silk merchants.
Key Historical Context: Tassini notes that the citizen family 'venuta da Milano, accumulò col traffico di panni di seta molte ricchezze' [Tassini 186], amassing a renowned art collection that included paintings by Antonello da Messina, Giorgione, and Bellini.
Tassini Work Cited: Alcuni palazzi ed antichi edifizii / Curiosità Veneziane
Exact Quotation from Tassini: venuta da Milano, accumulò col traffico di panni di seta molte ricchezze e costruì il magnifico palazzo.
English Translation & Toponymic Analysis: Having arrived from Milan, the family accumulated vast wealth through the silk trade and built a magnificent palace.

Location Name: Colonne della Piazzetta (Esecuzioni Capitali)
Description & Significance: The red granitoid columns of San Marco and San Todaro where public death sentences were carried out.
Key Historical Context: In his treatise *Condanne capitali a Venezia*, Tassini extracted the official *Registro dei giustiziati*, detailing execution methods (hanging, beheading, quartering) and superstitious beliefs that prevented Venetians from passing between the two columns [Tassini, Condanne].
Exact Quotation from Tassini: Il Registro dei giustiziati conservato alla Marciana e in copia alla Querini Stampalia ci offre il seguente quadro descritto dal Tassini.
English Translation & Toponymic Analysis: The Register of Executed Persons preserved at the Marciana offers the detailed record compiled and analyzed by Tassini.

Location Name: Isola del Lazzaretto Vecchio (I Lazzaretti della Peste)
Description & Significance: The world's first maritime plague quarantine station, established by the Venetian Senate.
Key Historical Context: Tassini provides a historical tally of epidemics in Venice, calculating that pestilence struck the lagoon city precisely 69 times between the Middle Ages and the 17th century [Tassini, Feste... 93].
Exact Quotation from Tassini: manifestandosi 69 volte [Cfr. Tassini, Feste... 93], ma fu alquanto rovinosa soprattutto nelle epidemie del 1576 e del 1630.
English Translation & Toponymic Analysis: Occurring 69 times according to Tassini's records, with the most catastrophic strikes in 1576 and 1630.

Location Name: Punta della Dogana (Torre di Difesa)
Description & Significance: The triangular tip of Dorsoduro guarding the entrance to the Grand and Giudecca Canals.
Key Historical Context: Tassini explains that before Giuseppe Benoni's 1677 customs house, the promontory was occupied by a battlemented military defense tower equipped with a heavy iron chain that stretched across the canal to San Marco to block enemy fleets [Tassini].
Exact Quotation from Tassini: già sistema difensivo della Repubblica con una torre merlata e sede degli Uffici della Dogana da Mar.
English Translation & Toponymic Analysis: Formerly a defensive fortification of the Republic featuring a crenellated tower and the maritime customs offices.

Location Name: Palazzo Savorgnan e Fondamenta Savorgnan
Description & Significance: Expansive Baroque palace and public park along the Cannaregio Canal, seat of the powerful Savorgnan condottieri.
Key Historical Context: Tassini documents the arrival of the Friulian Savorgnan dynasty into the patriciate in 1385 under Federico Savorgnan, and traces the naming of the fondamenta after their massive palace designed by Giuseppe Sardi [Tassini, Curiosità].
Exact Quotation from Tassini: Ascritta al M.C. con Federico nel 1385. Ebbe molti valorosi capitani al servizio della Serenissima.
English Translation & Toponymic Analysis: Enrolled in the Great Council with Federico in 1385, producing many valiant military commanders for the Republic.

Location Name: Palazzo Collalto (Scipione di Collalto)
Description & Significance: Venetian residence of the Counts of Collalto, lords of San Salvatore in Treviso.
Key Historical Context: Tassini records anecdotes regarding Count Scipione Vinciguerra di Collalto, who served the Republic in maritime campaigns and maintained an armed retinue in Venice [Tassini, Curiosità].
Exact Quotation from Tassini: Scipione di Collalto Vinciguerra, nobile e capitano di ventura ricordato negli aneddoti del Tassini.
English Translation & Toponymic Analysis: Scipione di Collalto Vinciguerra, nobleman and captain documented in Tassini's archival chronicles.

Location Name: Le Scoazzere di Venezia (Toponomastica Stradale)
Description & Significance: Walled municipal refuse enclosures built along canals where street sweepers (*nettadori di comun*) dumped garbage onto barges.
Key Historical Context: Tassini devotes multiple entries in *Curiosità Veneziane* to explaining why numerous alleys in Venice are called 'Calle della Scoazzera'. He describes the stone masonry pens created by the Giustizieri to prevent residents from dumping rubbish directly into the canals [Tassini, Curiosità].
Exact Quotation from Tassini: Le scoazzere erano recinti in muratura destinati al deposito delle immondizie prima di essere caricate sulle barche.
English Translation & Toponymic Analysis: The scoazzere were masonry pens designated for depositing street refuse before it was loaded onto barges.

Location Name: Palazzo Seriman (Ponte Seriman)
Description & Significance: Gothic-Baroque palace acquired by the wealthy Armenian Seriman family, giving its name to the salizada and bridge.
Key Historical Context: Tassini documents that the Seriman family, merchants hailing from Isfahan (Persia), bought the palace from the Bernardo family in 1701 for 30,000 ducats: 'I Seriman acquistarono nel 1701 il palazzo e diedero il nome alla salizzada e al ponte' [Tassini 708].
Exact Quotation from Tassini: I Seriman acquistarono nel 1701 il palazzo e diedero il nome alla salizzada e al ponte.
English Translation & Toponymic Analysis: The Seriman family purchased the palace in 1701 and gave their name to the salizada and the bridge.

Location Name: Palazzo Surian Bellotto
Description & Significance: Grand Renaissance palace on the Cannaregio Canal designed by Tullio Lombardo or Scarpagnino, later the French Embassy.
Key Historical Context: Tassini traces the history of the Surian family of originari citizens, which produced Grand Chancellor Andrea Surian and was admitted to the patriciate in 1648 for wartime financial contributions [Tassini]. Jean-Jacques Rousseau stayed here as secretary to the French ambassador in 1743.
Exact Quotation from Tassini: O Suriani, famiglia di cittadini originari, diede un cancelliere grande e fu assunta al patriziato per soldo.
English Translation & Toponymic Analysis: The Surian family of original citizens gave a Grand Chancellor and was elevated to the patriciate for funding wartime efforts.

Location Name: Chiesa e Convento delle Terese
Description & Significance: Carmelite convent and church founded in Dorsoduro by noblewoman Maria Ferrazzo for barefoot Carmelite nuns.
Key Historical Context: Tassini details the religious foundation established under the guidance of Father Bonaventura d'Este: 'Complesso composto da convento e chiesa, creato da Maria Ferrazzo sotto la direzione spirituale del carmelitano Bonaventura d'Este' [Tassini].
Tassini Work Cited: Edifici di Venezia distrutti e sconsacrati / Curiosità
Exact Quotation from Tassini: Complesso composto da convento e chiesa, creato da Maria Ferrazzo sotto la direzione spirituale del carmelitano Bonaventura.
English Translation & Toponymic Analysis: A complex composed of a convent and church created by Maria Ferrazzo under the spiritual guidance of Carmelite friar Bonaventura.

Location Name: Campo San Polo (Tiro a Segno dei Balestrieri)
Description & Significance: Open public field used by mandatory state decrees for weekly crossbow target training of all Venetian young men aged 16 to 35.
Key Historical Context: Tassini describes the public archery ranges where citizens practiced target shooting every Sunday under penalty of fines, establishing the physical layout of the targets until removed from Campo San Polo in 1452 [Tassini].
Exact Quotation from Tassini: Luoghi spaziosi per fare esercitare settimanalmente i veneziani maschi da 16 a 35 anni al tiro della balestra.
English Translation & Toponymic Analysis: Spacious fields designated for weekly crossbow shooting practice for Venetian males aged 16 to 35.

Location Name: Targa a Giuseppe Tassini (Lapidi Survey Record 0680)
Description & Significance: Marble commemorative epigraph cataloged in the Venice Project Center Inscriptions Survey (ObjectID 914 / Lapidi Row 681).
Key Historical Context: Official epigraph installed by the Municipality of Venice and Associazione Amici di Giuseppe Tassini on the centenary of his scholarship. Survey condition rating: 4/5 (fully legible).
Exact Quotation from Tassini: IN QUESTA CASA ABITÒ GIUSEPPE TASSINI AUTORE DELLE “CURIOSITÀ VENEZIANE” APPASSIONATO RICERCATORE DELLE NOSTRE TRADIZIONI 1827 – 1899.
English Translation & Toponymic Analysis: In this house lived Giuseppe Tassini, author of Curiosità Veneziane, passionate researcher of our traditions (1827–1899).

Location Name: Castello Ducale al Rivoalto (Origine del Palazzo Ducale)
Specific Location / Address: Piazzetta San Marco / Rio di Palazzo
Description & Significance: Founding year of the fortified ducal castle after the government relocated from Malamocco to Rivoalto.
Key Historical Context: Timeline event 814 cites Tassini's historical description of the original moated stronghold: 'Fondazione del Castello Ducale... Era un palazzo-fortezza, interamente circondato dall’acqua, con un ponte levatoio' [Tassini 378].
Exact Quotation from Tassini: Fondazione del Castello Ducale, poi Palazzo del Consiglio, cioè sede del Parlamento, e infine Palazzo Ducale [Cfr. Tassini 378].
English Translation & Toponymic Analysis: Foundation of the Ducal Castle, later the Palace of the Council, and ultimately the Doge's Palace as documented by Tassini.

Location Name: Chiese di San Lorenzo e San Severo (Isole Gemine)
Specific Location / Address: Campo San Lorenzo, 5069 / Campo San Severo
Description & Significance: Early medieval twin churches founded by Doge Angelo Partecipazio in the eastern lagoon islands.
Key Historical Context: Chronicle excerpt cited by Tassini: 'Chiese di San Lorenzo et San Severo fabricate dal Doge [Angelo Partecipazio], su l’Isole dette Gemine con molti alloggiamenti' [Tassini 387].
Exact Quotation from Tassini: Chiese di San Lorenzo et San Severo fabricate dal Doge [Angelo Partecipazio], su l’Isole dette Gemine con molti alloggiamenti.
English Translation & Toponymic Analysis: Churches of San Lorenzo and San Severo built by Doge Angelo Partecipazio on the islands called Gemine with multiple monastic quarters.

Location Name: Chiesa di Santa Maria Maddalena (Campo della Maddalena)
Description & Significance: Neoclassical circular church built by Tommaso Temanza on the site of a medieval 1222 foundation.
Key Historical Context: Tassini documents that the ancient church was refounded in 1222 by the Baffo family, who owned surrounding properties and held patronage rights [Tassini 400].
Exact Quotation from Tassini: Si rifonda la Chiesa di S.M. Maddalena, già esistente come è provato da un documento del 1155 [Cfr. Tassini 400].
English Translation & Toponymic Analysis: The Church of Santa Maria Maddalena was refounded, having existed prior as proven by an 1155 deed cited by Tassini.

Location Name: Ospizio Querini a San Giacomo dall'Orio
Description & Significance: Charitable hospice established by the Bishop of Castello for elderly impoverished Venetian citizens.
Key Historical Context: Tassini rectifies archival chronologies by demonstrating that Bishop Bartolomeo Querini's testament creating the hospice at San Giacomo dall'Orio dates to 1296 rather than 1291 [Tassini, Curiosità].
Exact Quotation from Tassini: Un lascito del vescovo di Castello, Bartolomeo Querini [Tassini scrive che il testamento è del 1296] assegna fondi per l'ospizio.
English Translation & Toponymic Analysis: A bequest from the Bishop of Castello, Bartolomeo Querini (which Tassini dates to 1296), provided funds for the hospice.

Location Name: Scuola dei Tintori a San Giovanni Grisostomo
Description & Significance: Confraternity hall of the cloth and silk dyers guild under the patronage of Sant'Onofrio.
Key Historical Context: Tassini records that the dyers gathered at San Giovanni Grisostomo, explaining how technical distinctions between dye types (*tintori di guado*, *tintori di grana*) shaped industrial streets like *Calle dei Tintori* and *Corte del Tintor* [Tassini, Curiosità].
Exact Quotation from Tassini: I tintori si raccolgono in una confraternita. Loro centro è la Scuola di S. Giovanni Grisostomo, il loro patrono sant’Onofrio.
English Translation & Toponymic Analysis: The dyers united into a brotherhood centered at the School of San Giovanni Grisostomo under patron saint Onuphrius.

Location Name: Campo Santa Maria Zobenigo (Morte di Luchino Visconti)
Description & Significance: Patrician palace near Santa Maria del Giglio where exiled Milanese lord Luchino Novello Visconti died.
Key Historical Context: Tassini records that Luchino Novello Visconti, who took refuge in Venice following his mother's death sentence in Milan, passed away here on July 7, 1399, and was given a solemn state funeral [Tassini 460].
Exact Quotation from Tassini: Muore Luchino Novello Visconti, che si era ritirato a Venezia dopo la condanna a morte della madre... [Cfr. Tassini 460].
English Translation & Toponymic Analysis: Death of Luchino Novello Visconti, who had retired to Venice after the death sentence of his mother, as cited by Tassini.

Location Name: Campo San Polo (Chiusura del Bersaglio dei Nobili)
Description & Significance: Removal of the archery butts from Venice's largest open square following complaints by noble residents.
Key Historical Context: Tassini cites the 1452 government decree shutting down target shooting in Campo San Polo: 'Si elimina il bersaglio d’arco e di balestre dal Campo S. Polo, avendo ciò ottenuto i nobili colà domiciliati in compenso delle spese fatte per selciarlo' [Tassini]. The square was paved and reserved for civic promenades.
Exact Quotation from Tassini: avendo ciò ottenuto i nobili colà domiciliati in compenso delle spese fatte per selciarlo.
English Translation & Toponymic Analysis: Noble residents obtained this closure as compensation for the private expenses they incurred to pave the square.

Location Name: Portico della Chiesa di Santa Maria Mater Domini
Description & Significance: Church portico closed by senate order to curb urban disorder and vagrancy.
Key Historical Context: Tassini cites the April 24, 1488 decree closing the portico: 'Si decreta che il portico della Chiesa di S.M. Mater Domini, ricettacolo, specialmente in tempo di notte, di scelleraggini e d’immondizie, venga chiuso con mura' [Tassini 420].
Exact Quotation from Tassini: Si decreta che il portico della Chiesa di S.M. Mater Domini, ricettacolo, specialmente in tempo di notte, di scelleraggini... venga chiuso.
English Translation & Toponymic Analysis: Decreed that the portico of the church, a nightly refuge for wickedness and filth, be permanently walled up.

Location Name: Piazza San Marco (Ricovero Invernale dei Barboni)
Specific Location / Address: Piazza San Marco / Scuderie del Palazzo Ducale
Description & Significance: Shelter in the ducal stables during the severe freeze of January 1506.
Key Historical Context: Tassini records that catastrophic winter frost froze the entire lagoon, prompting the Council of Ten to open the Doge's Palace stables and San Marco porticoes to prevent freezing deaths [Tassini].
Exact Quotation from Tassini: Per il gran freddo e la morte di molti barboni si decreta di ricoverare i poveri senza tetto presso le scuderie del doge.
English Translation & Toponymic Analysis: Due to the extreme cold and deaths among vagrants, authorities decreed that homeless persons be sheltered in the dogal stables.

Location Name: Chiesa dei Frari e Scuola di San Rocco (Regolamento Sepolture)
Description & Significance: Franciscan basilica and plague sanctuary regulating church burials.
Key Historical Context: Patriarch Gerolamo Querini's 1530 decree restricting burials inside sacred churches cited by Tassini, noting complaints about odors and health hazards that led to dedicated fraternity crypts [Tassini].
Exact Quotation from Tassini: Il patriarca Gerolamo Querini dichiara che le sepolture in chiesa devono essere riservate.
English Translation & Toponymic Analysis: Patriarch Querini decreed that burials within churches must be strictly restricted to specific patrons.

Location Name: Ospizio Nordio a Sant'Antonin
Description & Significance: Charity hospice founded by Bergamasque timber trader Bartolomeo Nordio.
Key Historical Context: Tassini documents that timber merchant Bartolomeo Nordio established the hospice for twelve poor indigent women in Salizada Sant'Antonin, endowing it with real estate revenues [Tassini 26].
Exact Quotation from Tassini: Un commerciante bergamasco di legnami (Bartolomeo Nordio) fonda a S. Antonin un ospizio per donne povere.
English Translation & Toponymic Analysis: A Bergamasque lumber trader (Bartolomeo Nordio) founded a shelter for impoverished women at Sant'Antonin.

Location Name: I Casoni di Sestiere (Cason di San Marco e San Polo)
Description & Significance: Neighborhood military guard stations and holding cells established in each sestiere.
Key Historical Context: Tassini analyzes a Maggior Consiglio deliberation of March 19, 1551, showing that every sestiere maintained a *cason* housing night guards (*sbirri*) and holding petty offenders, giving rise to street names like *Calle del Cason* [Tassini, Curiosità].
Exact Quotation from Tassini: Da una delibera del Maggior Consiglio apprendiamo che in ciascun sestiere si trova un cason, ovvero una prigione di custodia.
English Translation & Toponymic Analysis: From a Great Council resolution we learn that in each sestiere there was a cason, or municipal holding prison.

Location Name: I Ridotti di Venezia (Calle del Ridotto)
Description & Significance: Gaming and gambling houses operated by patricians across the city.
Key Historical Context: Tassini details the Senate prohibitions of February 27, 1567, which sought to crack down on private gaming casinos (*casin dei nobili*), noting that while officially forbidden, hundreds operated secretly under aristocratic immunity [Tassini, Curiosità].
Exact Quotation from Tassini: La Repubblica proibisce di tenere ridotti, altrimenti detti casin dei nobili, ma di fatto tenuti anche da ogni ceto sociale.
English Translation & Toponymic Analysis: The Republic forbade maintaining ridotti (casinos), though in reality they were operated across all social classes.

Location Name: Calle delle Carrozze a San Samuele
Description & Significance: Venetian street named after the workshops that built carriages for mainland export.
Key Historical Context: On the 1612 sentencing of Sebastian Bernardo for driving a carriage in town, Tassini clarifies why Venice has a *Calle delle Carrozze*: although carriages could not travel on Venetian canals and stepped bridges, luxury carriage builders maintained large assembly workshops here to export vehicles to mainland Italy [Tassini, Curiosità ... 142].
Exact Quotation from Tassini: A proposito delle carrozze, il Tassini scriverà che a Venezia non c’è l’uso ma se ne fabbricano per la terraferma.
English Translation & Toponymic Analysis: Regarding carriages, Tassini explains that they were not used in Venice, but were manufactured here for export to the terraferma.

Location Name: Calle de le Rasse (Origine del Nome)
Description & Significance: Historic alley off the Riva degli Schiavoni near the Doge's Palace.
Key Historical Context: In connection with the apothecary shop of Sante Gariboldi, Tassini explains the toponymy: 'la rassa o rascia è, secondo il Tassini, un panno di lana ordinaria con quale si coprono i felzi delle gondole, panno originario di Rascia (Serbia)' [Tassini, Curiosità ... 584].
Exact Quotation from Tassini: la rassa o rascia è, secondo il Tassini, un panno di lana ordinaria con quale si coprono i felzi delle gondole.
English Translation & Toponymic Analysis: La rassa or rascia is, according to Tassini, a coarse wool fabric originating from Rascia (Serbia) used to cover gondola canopies.

Location Name: Fondamente Nove (Fondazione di Santa Maria del Pianto)
Description & Significance: Northern waterfront of Venice overlooking the cemetery island and Murano.
Key Historical Context: Timeline record of the foundation of Santa Maria del Pianto cites Tassini's history of how the monastery survived until Napoleonic suppression, when it was bought for schools [Tassini].
Exact Quotation from Tassini: Si fonda all’estremità delle Fondamente Nove, a fianco di un convento di monache cappuccine, la Chiesa di S.M. del Pianto.
English Translation & Toponymic Analysis: Founded at the eastern tip of Fondamente Nove, beside a Capuchin convent, the Church of Santa Maria del Pianto.

Location Name: Corte del Brusà in Barbarìa de le Tole
Specific Location / Address: Corte del Brusà / Barbarìa de le Tole, 6420
Description & Significance: Courtyard named after the catastrophic fire of 1686 that destroyed lumber yards and 70 houses.
Key Historical Context: Tassini records the terrible blaze in the timber warehouses destined for North Africa (Barbaria), noting that only a single home miraculously survived: 'È fama che allora restasse illesa dalle fiamme una sola casa, e ciò venne attribuito ad un miracolo di S. Antonio' [Tassini 660], naming the site *Corte del Brusà* ('Courtyard of the Burned').
Exact Quotation from Tassini: È fama che allora restasse illesa dalle fiamme una sola casa, e ciò venne attribuito ad un miracolo di S. Antonio.
English Translation & Toponymic Analysis: Legend holds that only one house was left undamaged by the flames, attributed to a miracle of Saint Anthony; hence the name Corte del Brusà.

Location Name: Campanile di San Marco (Loggetta del Lotto)
Description & Significance: Sansovino's loggetta at the base of the Campanile where public lotto drawings occurred.
Key Historical Context: Tassini documents the revival of the state lottery: on April 5, 1734, the first drawing of the reformed lotto was celebrated publicly from the Loggetta of San Marco to raise state revenues [Tassini 514].
Exact Quotation from Tassini: Prima estrazione del rinnovato Gioco del Lotto, nato con un decreto del 14 gennaio 1733 [Cfr. Tassini 514].
English Translation & Toponymic Analysis: First drawing of the reformed Lotto game, established by decree to raise state funds, cited by Tassini.

Location Name: Ponte di Rialto (Spezieria Talamini)
Description & Significance: Stone bridge arches where Giambattista Talamini exhibited his botanical art.
Key Historical Context: Timeline entry confirms Tassini's chronicle that on April 17, 1757, Talamini's apothecary shop attracted international visitors for its uncanny wax fruits [Tassini].
Exact Quotation from Tassini: Da Gio. Battista Talamini, che ha una bottega da speziale sul Ponte di Rialto, si vende frutta di cera che sembra vera.
English Translation & Toponymic Analysis: At the shop of apothecary Giambattista Talamini on the Rialto Bridge, wax fruits were sold that looked completely genuine.

Location Name: Calle dei Barbieri a San Marco (Moda delle Parrucche)
Description & Significance: Guild street of 18th-century hairdressers and peruke makers.
Key Historical Context: Tassini reports 1762 census figures showing over 700 barber-wigmakers in Venice styling expensive powdered white wigs for aristocrats and magistrates [Tassini, Curiosità].
Exact Quotation from Tassini: Risulta che a Venezia i parrucchieri e i barbieri che arricciano e pettinano parrucche sono centinaia...
English Translation & Toponymic Analysis: Records show hundreds of hairdressers and wig stylists active in Venice, documented by Tassini.

Location Name: Campanile dei Santi Apostoli
Description & Significance: Towering bell tower struck by lightning on October 28, 1779.
Key Historical Context: Tassini recounts the miraculous escape of priest Domenico Longo during the tower's 1672 construction: Longo slipped from the high scaffolding, but his flowing cassock snagged on a wooden beam, leaving him dangling safely until builders pulled him up: 'Colà rimase per buona sorte sospeso quanto bastò perché si potesse accorrere in suo aiuto, e salvarlo' [Tassini, Curiosità ... 36].
Exact Quotation from Tassini: Colà rimase per buona sorte sospeso quanto bastò perché si potesse accorrere in suo aiuto, e salvarlo.
English Translation & Toponymic Analysis: There he remained fortunately suspended long enough for aid to reach him and save his life.

Location Name: Le Mercerie (Moti Antigiacobini del Maggio 1797)
Description & Significance: Primary commercial street connecting Piazza San Marco to Rialto, site of urban clashes during the fall of the Republic.
Key Historical Context: Tassini provides an eyewitness-grounded description of loyalist anti-Jacobin riots: 'Appena dunque che questi, per nulla intimoriti, s’avvicinarono tumultuando, davasi fuoco alle miccie, e la via sottoposta riempivasi di sanguinosi cadaveri' [Tassini, Curiosità ... 62].
Exact Quotation from Tassini: davasi fuoco alle miccie, e la via sottoposta riempivasi di sanguinosi cadaveri.
English Translation & Toponymic Analysis: Matches were touched to fuses, and the street below was filled with bloody casualties as the populace revolted.

Location Name: Sant'Alvise / Calle de le Muneghe (Tragedia Lovat)
Description & Significance: Timeline record of shoemaker Matteo Lovat's religious martyrdom spectacle.
Key Historical Context: Chronological entry reiterating Tassini's documentation of Matteo Lovat's self-crucifixion in Calle de le Muneghe, noting that the crowd gathered in horror before cutting him down and taking him to San Servolo hospital [Tassini, Curiosità ... 439].
Exact Quotation from Tassini: Fa scalpore in città la notizia che il calzolaio Matteo Lovat, abitante in Calle de le Muneghe a S. Alvise al civico 3281... si era crocifisso.
English Translation & Toponymic Analysis: Sensational news spread that shoemaker Matteo Lovat, living in Calle de le Muneghe at number 3281, had crucified himself.

Location Name: Quartiere di Sant'Antonio a Castello (Creazione Giardini)
Description & Significance: Demolition of the historic fishermen's parish of Sant'Antonio for public parklands.
Key Historical Context: Timeline entry citing Tassini's account of how the historic quarter, gothic monasteries, and working-class fishermen homes were completely razed under French rule: 'Ad ottenere lo spazio necessario, si distrussero le parrocchie...' [Tassini, Curiosità ... 277].
Exact Quotation from Tassini: Inizia la demolizione del quartiere di S. Antonio a Castello e la creazione dei Giardini Pubblici (1807-10).
English Translation & Toponymic Analysis: Demolition of the Sant'Antonio quarter in Castello and creation of the Public Gardens began in 1807, cited by Tassini.

Location Name: Ponte della Paglia e Ponte della Pietà
Description & Significance: Promenade bridges along Riva degli Schiavoni connecting San Marco to Castello.
Key Historical Context: Tassini records that the municipal government decided to widen the Ponte della Paglia and Ponte della Pietà to accommodate expanding pedestrian crowds along the waterfront; works commenced in 1847 and concluded in 1854 [Tassini 473].
Exact Quotation from Tassini: Si decide di allargare il Ponte della Paglia e quello della Pietà. I lavori cominciano nel 1847 e saranno completati nel 1854 [Cfr. Tassini 473].
English Translation & Toponymic Analysis: Decided to widen Ponte della Paglia and Ponte della Pietà; works began in 1847 and were completed in 1854, recorded by Tassini.

Location Name: Riva degli Schiavoni (Protesta Toponomastica di Tassini)
Description & Significance: Major maritime promenade of Venice, subject of civic debate on street prostitution.
Key Historical Context: Tassini writes in the later editions of *Curiosità Veneziane* calling for an overhaul of prostitution laws, decrying how public promenades like Riva degli Schiavoni were compromised by open solicitation [Tassini, Curiosità].
Exact Quotation from Tassini: Il Tassini scrive nelle sue Curiosità veneziane che si spera in una riforma della legge sulla prostituzione perché le meretrici invadono tutti i luoghi pubblici.
English Translation & Toponymic Analysis: Tassini writes in Curiosità Veneziane that he hopes for a reform of prostitution laws because courtesans occupied public promenades.

Location Name: Lido di Venezia - Alberoni / Quattro Fontane (Duello Macola)
Description & Significance: Chronicle entry of duel between student Galli and journalist Ferruccio Macola.
Key Historical Context: Tassini records the second duel won by Macola and laments the failure of police enforcement against premeditated aristocratic duels [Tassini, Curiosità ... XXVI].
Exact Quotation from Tassini: Quest’ultimo in ambidue rimase vincitore... come va che si compiono in barba all'autorità.
English Translation & Toponymic Analysis: Macola remained victor in both; Tassini questions why these duels occurred openly in defiance of the law.

Location Name: Casa e Morte di Giuseppe Tassini (22 Dicembre 1899)
Description & Significance: Official timeline entry for the passing of Giuseppe Tassini at his home near Piazza San Marco.
Key Historical Context: Tassini passes away at age 72. Timeline documents: 'Muore a 72 anni il veneziano Giuseppe Tassini (1827-99) e una lapide marmorea posta nel 1988 sul muro della casa in cui visse (Calle dei Specchieri 635/634) lo ricorda come appassionato ricercatore delle nostre tradizioni' [Distefano Atlante 701].
Exact Quotation from Tassini: Muore a 72 anni il veneziano Giuseppe Tassini (1827-99) e una lapide marmorea posta nel 1988 sul muro della casa in cui visse lo ricorda.
English Translation & Toponymic Analysis: Giuseppe Tassini died at age 72; a marble plaque installed in 1988 on his home in Calle dei Spechieri commemorates him as a passionate researcher of traditions.
